title: page-fence evictor and tenant slack reservation to reduce fragmentation and spillover
author: Noah Singh
release_notes: Introduces a page-fence based evictor and tenant-level slack reservation to reduce high-fragmentation-induced spillovers. Improves steady-state tail latency by reducing reactive paging under bursty workloads. No API changes.
description:
Motivation:
High-fragmentation scenarios in multi-tenant KV pools were triggering large, reactive spillovers and multi-page churn that elevated tail latency and cost. Existing eviction heuristics aggressively greedified hot tenants or compacted large ranges, which worked poorly when small, interleaved allocations prevented contiguous reclaim. This PR adds a page-fence evictor and tenant slack reservation mechanism to provide smoother reclaim behavior, pre-emptive micro-reclamation windows, and tighter integration with the continuous batching scheduler.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a page-fence eviction algorithm that marks soft fences around hot ranges and prefers fenced-localized reclamation to reduce cross-range fragmentation.
- Introduces tenant-level slack reservations (configurable per-tenant) so tenants keep a small working-set buffer that avoids immediate spillover when transient bursts occur.
- Hooks the evictor into the continuous batching scheduler so reclamation work is batched with background kernel scheduling cycles to avoid latency spikes.
- Provides a gentle degradation mode: when global pressure is high, the evictor expands fence windows gradually and triggers cooperative eviction across tenants.
- Tests, benchmarks, and operational docs for on-call tuning.

Implementation notes (high level commits):
- commit 1: implement page_fence_evictor core loop, estimate fragmentation score per-page and fence creation heuristics.
- commit 2: tenant_slack reservation API and persistence; per-tenant token bucket-style slack ledger.
- commit 3: scheduler integration: continuous_batching: schedule_reclaim_hook and low-priority reclaim worker.
- commit 4: telemetry: metrics for fence_count, fence_hit_ratio, slack_consumption, and spillover_events.
- commit 5: unit/integration tests and a small e2e benchmark harness under test/kv_fence_bench.*

Files changed (high-level):
- kv/evictor/page_fence_evictor.rs - new algorithm and core logic (approx 480 lines).
- kv/allocator/tenant_slack.rs - reservation ledger and API hooks.
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.rs - hook to schedule reclaim windows and backoff policy.
- tests/unit/test_page_fence.rs - unit tests for fence creation and scoring.
- tests/integration/kv_stress_slack.py - integration script to validate spillover behavior under mixed tenants.
- docs/operational/kv_tuning.md - guidance for tenant slack sizing and fence thresholds.
- observability/metrics/registry.yaml - added new metrics and alert knobs.

Behavioral details and knobs:
- page_fence_evictor computes a per-page fragmentation score using occupancy variance and neighbor-free-run-length. Fences are created when localized fragmentation exceeds the configured fence_threshold (default 0.65). Fences are soft: they bias reclaim decisions but do not hard-pin pages.
- tenant_slack is a small soft-reservation expressed in pages (default 4 pages) and can be configured per-tenant via ControlPlane configs. Slack is drawn down during bursts and replenishes at a small steady rate; if a tenant exhausts slack and global pressure is high, they become eligible for cooperative reclaim.
- Scheduler integration ensures reclamation work is grouped into the low-priority continuous batching pass. This prevents per-request latency interference by performing defrag/reclaim work in micro-batches between request batches.

Benchmarks and results (summary):
- micro-bench (10 tenants, 50% hot working set): tail P99 latency reduced by ~22% vs master under identical GC/evictor settings.
- spillover event frequency reduced by ~55% on synthetic fragmentation traces (small, interleaved allocations).
- small throughput regression (approx 0.8%) observed under extreme global pressure due to additional reclaim work; mitigated by tuning reclaim_backoff_ms and fence expansion rate. Detailed numbers in docs/operational/kv_tuning.md.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for fence scoring and slack ledger (coverage added).
- Integration stress test across 1000 simulated tenants and a replay of production hotspot traces (redwood/bench/replays/trace-2026-01-10).
- Canary rollout over dedicated cluster: watched memory metrics, fence_hit_ratio, and spillover_events for 48h. No customer-visible errors.

Migration/compatibility:
- No external API changes. Tenant slack defaults are benign; operators must opt-in via ControlPlane to increase/decrease slack.
- If older control planes do not supply tenant slack settings, the default runtime behavior remains compatible.

Operational guidance (short):
1) Start with default fence_threshold=0.65 and tenant_slack_pages=4.
2) For tenant bursts with frequent small allocations, increase slack to 8 pages and reduce fence_threshold to 0.55.
3) If reclaim work increases CPU at peak, increase reclaim_backoff_ms or throttle reclaim windows in the ControlPlane rollout.
